links.outcome: Diagnostic performance difference between successive ChatGPT versions on audiogram interpretation
links.effect: ChatGPT-5.1 scored significantly higher than ChatGPT-4.0 on 6 of 7 questions (P < .001), effect sizes 0.53 to 0.94; bone conduction item showed no significant difference (P = .121).
links.quote: ChatGPT-5.1 scored significantly higher than ChatGPT-4.0 on 6 of 7 questions (P < .001), with effect sizes ranging from 0.53 to 0.94.

links.outcome: Model performance on audiograms with intentional masking errors (flawed inputs)
links.effect: Both models performed poorly on audiograms containing masking errors (20 of 100 audiograms had intentional masking errors).
links.quote: Both models performed poorly on audiograms containing masking errors.

screen.reason: The study is an empirical benchmark comparing the diagnostic performance of two versions of ChatGPT on simulated audiogram interpretation without testing a deployment safeguard or practice.
